news.title: Nvidia suspends server shipments to Southeast Asia
news.description: Nvidia reportedly asked server manufacturers to stop deliveries to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after new US export rules took effect. Fitch expects slower growth and more selective investment in data centers across the region.

news.title: Display projected range again as a number on a Tesla
news.description: On a 2025 Tesla Model 3, projected range was previously displayed numerically. A software update now displays it as a graph.

news.title: Discussion of Model 3 mechanical and hardware problems
news.description: A member describes an issue with their Tesla Model 3 and asks the community for help. The excerpt repeats the question about range display after a software update.

news.title: 42 attorneys general oppose the sale of Character.AI conversations
news.description: A bipartisan coalition of 42 US attorneys general is trying to block the planned sale of conversation histories from more than 21 million accounts. It denounces the lack of safeguards allowing users to delete data or requiring buyers to follow privacy policies.

news.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist proposes common limits for AI
news.description: Jakub Pachocki published the pretraining scores of OpenAI’s leading models since GPT-3.5 and asked competing labs to adopt common limits. Sam Altman called the proposal OpenAI’s most important publication in some time.

news.title: AI agents are making self-hosting accessible again
news.description: Integrating AI programming agents into infrastructure management reduces routine tasks and makes it easier to experiment with technologies such as NixOS. It also enables automated deployments and makes it easier to create custom tools.

news.title: OpenAI appears to be cutting the costs of its models
news.description: Astra 6.2 and Sol 6.2 appear to have been optimized to reduce costs, with a sharp drop in output and reasoning tokens per task. These models seem to reason significantly less than their competitors.

news.title: Alleged breakthrough in quantum gravity called into question
news.description: A recent article by an OpenAI employee claiming to have quantified gravity went viral on X. For now, however, it appears that AI has not solved the quantum gravity problem.

news.title: Katie Notopoulos has built a reputation for scolding AI
news.description: Katie Notopoulos is known for firmly scolding artificial intelligence agents.

news.title: Elon Musk mentions a potential 128 quintillion valuation for SpaceX
news.description: Elon Musk cited a potential valuation of 128 quintillion dollars for SpaceX.

news.title: OpenAI claims to have found the exact limit of matrix multiplication
news.description: OpenAI published a preprint claiming that the minimal exponent for matrix multiplication is exactly 9/4, or 2.25. The result concerns gigantic matrices and would not provide an immediate practical speedup; experts still need to verify the proof.

news.title: Study cites MiniMax after private links were opened in AI queries
news.description: Dragos researcher HD Moore cited MiniMax in a study about unidentified parties opening private links embedded in queries sent to AIs.

news.title: Study finds that AI licenses are not yet transforming companies
news.description: An AI Questions presentation argues that giving every employee an AI license spreads the technology without changing how the company operates. Around 45% of U.S. workers use generative AI at work, but fewer than 15% use it daily.

news.title: OpenAI fixes a bug that reduced GPT-6.2 quotas
news.description: A billing bug gave discounts to most ChatGPT subscribers. After it was fixed, usage limits are reached 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol, with no retroactive billing.

news.title: Scott Aaronson believes labs are hiding cryptographic breakthroughs
news.description: Former OpenAI researcher Scott Aaronson says several mathematical results produced by AI are important and is almost certain that labs are keeping cryptographic “bombs” hidden. He also writes that, for the first time, he feels a proof that P ≠ NP may not be far away.

news.title: ChatGPT boosts consultants’ performance without increasing their expertise
news.description: According to a study analyzed by Towards Data Science, consultants assisted by ChatGPT gained 49 points on programming tasks without developing a better understanding of the subject. Apprentices also improved their understanding.

news.title: Elon Musk promises one SpaceX share per year to every American child
news.description: After donating one SpaceX share to the roughly 70 million child savings accounts known as “Trump Accounts,” Elon Musk promised to give one to every American child each year. The stock gained 7.47% in overnight trading.

news.title: Pinterest lets parents limit the AI content teenagers see
news.description: Pinterest is introducing a new parental-control center with a setting for the volume of AI-generated content, along with options for autoplay and notifications. A passcode protects these settings, but some synthetic content may still get through the filter.

news.title: Tesla owners discuss range anxiety
news.description: The exchange focuses on electric-vehicle range anxiety and ways to overcome it during long trips.

news.title: Could camera cleaning become routine maintenance?
news.description: Tesla owners are wondering whether the vehicles’ cameras need to be cleaned regularly.

news.title: An owner believes they have found a solution to Tesla frustrations
news.description: A Tesla owner says a solution was found thanks to a 14-minute YouTube video published by “TechGeek Tesla.”

news.title: A buyer’s doubts before taking delivery of their Tesla
news.description: A buyer is wondering whether they should still take delivery of their Tesla. They can cancel the order if their concerns outweigh the benefits.

news.title: An owner seeks support before their main battery is replaced
news.description: An owner is asking for reassurance while Tesla replaces their vehicle’s main battery. The battery is now at 0% and the trunks are open, which could indicate that the work has begun.

news.title: Discussion of Tesla-only Superchargers
news.description: The discussion concerns Tesla’s promotion of its own products and services, particularly its Supercharger network, which is integrated into its ecosystem.

news.title: Limits of FSD assistance when the driver intervenes
news.description: An exchange criticizes the lack of a sufficiently gradual exit from FSD mode and the “Why did you intervene” message.

news.title: Tesla key cards work to start the car but not to lock it
news.description: A Model 3 owner says both key cards work when placed behind the cup holder to drive, but not to lock or unlock the car.

news.title: User compares FSD Lite with a more capable HW4 version
news.description: A user says they have version 2026.44.1 with FSD 14.3 Lite, which they consider less capable than version 14 tested on a vehicle equipped with HW4.

news.title: Discussion of the shape of Tesla jack adapters
news.description: The discussion clarifies that the adapter’s stem goes into the car’s chassis, while the other side depends on the jack being used.

news.title: Treg launches an API that can reconstruct a person’s digital profile
news.description: Treg’s People API allows AI agents to search a person’s digital life for $0.07 per query. Presented as a prospecting tool, the service is raising privacy concerns.

news.title: Claude can create an app to clean CSV exports
news.description: The tutorial suggests using Claude and its Artifacts to create an interactive app that can preview, clean and download CSV files. The tool can remove duplicates and blank rows, normalize spacing, capitalization and dates, and summarize the changes made.

news.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chairman and CEO
news.description: Nvidia’s board unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as chairman, CEO and a board member, less than two weeks after his resignation. It says it consulted senior US government officials and sees no national security risk.

news.title: An Anthropic mathematician claims to have proved the Riemann hypothesis
news.description: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge published a formal proof of the Riemann hypothesis, an unsolved problem since 1859. He claims Claude got him most of the way through the final step.

news.title: Anthropic lets users install Claude Artifacts as desktop apps
news.description: Anthropic now allows Artifacts to be installed as custom applications on Mac and Windows. Users can ask Claude to create an Artifact, choose “Install as app” and set its privacy limits.

news.title: Epochal launches Time Portal, a time machine for AI agents
news.description: Epochal, a startup founded by former xAI employees, introduced Time Portal. The service confines AI agents to the state of the Internet on a given date over the past thirty years or more so they can produce forecasts.

news.title: A presentation rewrites itself live with the Opus 5.6 model
news.description: A creator claims to have submitted an ordinary presentation to the unreleased Opus 5.6 model and watched it rewrite itself while being displayed. The demonstration received 39,000 likes.

news.title: A viral prompt pushes AI models to deepen their responses
news.description: A prompt asks the model not merely to “improve” a text, but to reason like a top-level professional. According to the newsletter, this change can substantially improve response quality.

news.title: Engineers reportedly managed to run GTA 6 on PC
news.description: Reverse-engineering specialists reportedly managed to run GTA 6 on PC despite the lack of an official version. The breakthrough reportedly angered Rockstar’s parent company.

news.title: SAP and planqc prepare to integrate quantum computing into business software
news.description: SAP believes quantum computing could become useful for its business software before the end of the decade. Tests of planqc’s hardware are scheduled for 2027.

news.title: Can small IT teams afford conversational help desks?
news.description: ServiceNow launched Flow, a conversational service desk capable of handling IT requests in Slack and Microsoft Teams. Small and midsize teams nevertheless face high prices, unpredictable billing and risks of complexity or service disruption.

news.title: KubeCon 2026 focuses on AI traffic management and Ingress-NGINX migration
news.description: At KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026, discussions focused on AI traffic management and migration paths following the discontinuation of Ingress-NGINX. NGINX presented migration tools, controls for AI gateways and policy-as-code templates.

news.title: Canonical announces new Ubuntu integrations on Azure at Ignite 2026
news.description: Canonical announced new Ubuntu integrations with Azure services, including the general availability of Azure Cobalt 200 virtual machines and Microsoft Foundry Managed Compute with Ubuntu Pro security patches. Other announcements concern Azure App Service, the Azure Marketplace and several preview features.

news.title: AI models should be managed like software dependencies
news.description: Large language models should follow software supply-chain governance practices to limit behavioral drift, transitive dependencies and security risks. Recommended practices include locking configurations, statistical testing and creating an AI software bill of materials.

news.title: Expo lets developers deploy a production fix from a phone
news.description: Developers can diagnose bugs, create pull requests and verify fixes from a mobile device using AI assistants and Expo MCP servers. Approved fixes can then be deployed to users through over-the-air updates.

news.title: easyDNS urges immediate renewal of AWS keys stored in its panel
news.description: easyDNS is asking users who store their AWS keys in the control panel for Route53 integration to renew them immediately. The recommendation follows reports of compromised keys.

news.title: SAP considers eliminating at least 10,000 jobs in its AI-related restructuring
news.description: The job cuts would affect approximately 9% of SAP’s global workforce. The final number still depends on negotiations with employee representatives.

news.title: Nvidia chip buyers must exclude Chinese renters
news.description: A new US rule aims to prevent Chinese companies from remotely renting the most advanced Nvidia chips hosted abroad. Sellers told neoclouds they would not be able to buy Nvidia chips if part of their capacity was rented to Chinese companies.

news.title: China’s second-largest pork producer adopts livestock robots
news.description: Wens Foodstuff Group invested in Lasaite Robot, which makes robots that travel on rails inside livestock buildings. These robots monitor pigs’ body temperature, feeding and activity to detect diseases or other health problems early.

news.title: MCP could see a renewed surge in 2027
news.description: After the initial enthusiasm, backlash and confusion surrounding MCP, sentiment is shifting again. Protocol traffic is increasing, while MCP continues to advance and customers are using it more intelligently.

news.title: Multi-agent software development could transform the industry
news.description: Multi-agent development could have a major impact on the software industry and intellectual work in general. Experiments are already showing how collaboration between agents could work, but autonomous agents also pose risks when interacting with infrastructure.

news.title: Human intelligence remains indispensable despite AI advances
news.description: Despite their recent progress, cutting-edge AIs remain limited by the human talent needed to improve them. Many characteristics of human intelligence are still major goals for AI labs.

news.title: The Jevons paradox is losing momentum in AI
news.description: Token consumption continues to rise, but spending growth has slowed sharply in recent months. Falling token prices are therefore leading less clearly to an increase in total inference spending.

news.title: Memory chip shortages drive up gift prices
news.description: End-of-year gifts will cost more this year because chips are becoming scarcer.

news.title: Restrictions on agents’ access to accounts risk being bypassed
news.description: Companies are putting policies in place to prevent agents from accessing their information. However, these attempts to preserve the status quo will eventually be bypassed as technologies advance and agents become more effective with browsers.

news.title: Interface design is evolving in the age of AI
news.description: Interface design is not limited to drawing buttons, and designers are finally beginning to realize it.

news.title: Language models are becoming more capable and cheaper
news.description: Large language models are gaining capabilities while costing less, but companies’ bills are not falling.

news.title: Explicit errors make software diagnosis easier
news.description: Errors should contain enough information to help explain how the software failed.

news.title: AI safety experts plan their finances around extinction risk
news.description: Business Insider asked AI safety experts how likely an AI-caused catastrophe is and how it influences their financial decisions.

news.title: Black Friday becomes a major test for AI shopping agents
news.description: Black Friday is putting AI shopping agents to the test, as a single bad order could be enough to undermine users’ trust.

news.title: Black Friday discounts are finally becoming worthwhile
news.description: Black Friday has arrived, and discounts are expected to become significantly more appealing.

news.title: The first agent-driven Black Friday begins
news.description: Black Friday is becoming a real-world test for AI agents tasked with making purchases.

news.title: An AI agent orders 20 pounds of chicken instead of dinner for two
news.description: A user asked an AI agent to order dinner for two, but the agent ordered 20 pounds of chicken wings.

news.title: An AI agent adds a $250.75 suitcase to an unsolicited list
news.description: An agent sent a user an unsolicited shopping list that included, among other things, a $250.75 suitcase.

news.title: Muse agent tries to charge a salad to an HSA card
news.description: The Muse agent tried to charge Katie Notopoulos’s salad to her HSA card.

news.title: An AI agent shares an address and arranges an unexpected meetup
news.description: A user says an agent shared his address with a buyer and arranged a pickup, before a man showed up at his home.

news.title: AI-related traffic could double during Black Friday
news.description: Traffic from AI agents to commerce sites is expected to double during Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

news.title: Global markets rise after Thanksgiving
news.description: U.S. futures and global markets are rising as part of a post-Thanksgiving rebound.

news.title: Business leaders describe a golden age for builders
news.description: Business leaders explain what they are grateful for this year, with some describing a “golden age for builders.”

news.title: AI is changing how engineers get promoted
news.description: An Anthropic team leader says AI is changing how engineers earn promotions.

news.title: How MrBeast became YouTube’s biggest creator
news.description: The article traces Jimmy Donaldson’s journey from a reserved childhood to building a multibillion-dollar business.

news.title: Young Americans are betting on stocks to build wealth
news.description: Young Americans are relying on stocks to build their wealth, but one economist believes a risk could undermine this strategy.

news.title: Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia gives Denny’s a marketing boost
news.description: Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia created a viral marketing opportunity for restaurant chain Denny’s.

news.title: The vehicles that shaped Waymo’s robotaxi fleet
news.description: Waymo’s self-driving cars evolved from desert racing vehicles to luxury SUVs. The article looks back at the models that shaped its robotaxi fleet.

news.title: DOGE cuts push two government officials into politics
news.description: DOGE-led cuts pushed government officials to enter politics, and two of them have just been elected to Congress.

news.title: Minecraft’s reclusive creator makes Anthropic a proposal
news.description: Minecraft’s creator, known for keeping a low profile, has made Anthropic a proposal.

news.title: An architect leaves her field to work at Sweetgreen
news.description: The author recounts leaving a career in architecture to work at Sweetgreen, a choice she does not regret.

news.title: Prototype lets users dictate prompts to Claude Code by lip-reading
news.description: Lip Dictation reads lip movements through a Mac’s webcam and turns silently mouthed words into a prompt. Processing remains local, but accuracy is limited, especially for technical terms.

news.title: Open-source model improves its Lao translation without losing Thai performance
news.description: Together AI trained Qwen3.8-27B on Lao examples, but the improvement initially severely degraded Thai. Adding around 1,000 Thai translations generated by Kimi-K3.1-Pro preserved performance in both languages.

news.title: Z.AI delays GLM-5.5 launch amid restrictions on access to computing
news.description: Z.AI has reportedly fallen behind schedule on the launch of GLM-5.5. Moonshot also said that the gap between its major releases could double if the company lost access to computing capacity overseas.

news.title: Investigation finds undisclosed AI use in 25 court cases
news.description: The Bureau of Investigative Journalism found undisclosed AI use in at least 25 cases in England and Wales. Some rulings included fabricated case law and nonexistent statutes.

news.title: Huawei claims double the density for new high-bandwidth memory
news.description: Huawei researchers have scheduled a paper on a memory chip for presentation at a conference in February. They claim data density twice that of South Korean competitors’ high-bandwidth memory, but actual production remains uncertain.

news.title: Robotera deploys 45 humanoid robots to sort parcels in China
news.description: Robotera says 45 humanoid robots were involved in parcel processing at a China Post facility in Hangzhou. Their throughput improved during the pilot phase.

news.title: DeepL launches Aure v2, a voice translator with half the latency
news.description: Aure v2 directly translates speech from one language into speech in another in a single step. The model cuts latency in half compared with the previous version and supports six languages for existing DeepL Voice customers.

news.title: Statista puts some of its data behind a barrier to AI bots
news.description: Statista placed most of its data behind a sign-up requirement to prevent AI bots from crawling it. Its search traffic fell from around 35 million to 8 million monthly users, but its CEO is betting on the value of fresh, traceable data.

news.title: GPT-6.2 Astra identifies the creator of an anonymous sketchbook in 22 minutes
news.description: Historian Mark Humphries reports that GPT-6.2 Astra identified the creator of an anonymous sketchbook from 1808 in the Yale archives. The model found a mention in a little-known archival journal, raising concerns about AI’s ability to conduct historical research.

news.title: Simon Willison describes three capability leaps in AI models over one year
news.description: Simon Willison identifies the arrival of reliable coding agents in late 2025, models capable of solving problems through persistence this summer, and models handling 3D and game design this fall. In his view, a leading model can now create software whose specifications are clearly described.

news.title: Claude Opus 5.6 is reportedly being secretly tested with some users
news.description: Testers attribute short films and fully code-produced 3D scenes to an unannounced model nicknamed Opus-next or Claude Opus 5.6. Anthropic has not confirmed anything, and there is no official benchmark, pricing or release schedule.

news.title: Bionic hand lets patient feel touch at home
news.description: A LUKE bionic hand connected to forearm nerves allows Avi Davidson to control his prosthesis and feel pressure. He is the first trial patient to use it independently in everyday life at home.

news.title: Q.ANT develops photonic chips to reduce AI energy use
news.description: German startup Q.ANT is developing processors that compute with light waves rather than electrons. Its chips are being tested at IONOS, and more than 30 teams are designing compatible models.

news.title: llama.cpp releases dashboard for measuring local AI on AMD
news.description: The llama.cpp project offers a dashboard on Hugging Face for comparing model speeds by AMD hardware, version and quantization. Tests include the Radeon 8060S and Radeon AI Pro R9700S.

news.title: Baidu reportedly releases open weights for ERNIE 5.5 Flash
news.description: According to the AI Secret newsletter, Baidu has reportedly made ERNIE 5.5 Flash available with open weights. The model’s size, license and performance could not be verified.

news.title: Coding agents renew interest in self-hosting
news.description: One enthusiast explains that AI coding agents let him adopt NixOS in half a day instead of a week. They also help him track versions, update containers and deploy his services.

news.title: last30days-skill automates monitoring of Reddit, X and YouTube
news.description: This open-source project adds a research skill to an AI agent for Reddit, X, YouTube, Hacker News, Polymarket and the web. It then produces a summary accompanied by verifiable sources.

news.title: Man sentenced to 47 months in prison for cloning a streamer’s voice
news.description: David Anthony Sanchez used an AI-cloned voice to impersonate streamer N3on and promote a fake memecoin project. Victims paid around $260,000 in cryptocurrency.

news.title: Chinese labs delay models amid shortages of chips and distillation restrictions
news.description: Z.AI is reportedly pushing GLM-5.5 back to the first quarter of 2027 and will release GLM-5.4 in the meantime. Moonshot AI could double its development cycle, while restrictions on distillation and access to GPUs complicate its work.

news.title: Nvidia threatens to cut shipments to clouds renting capacity to China
news.description: Nvidia chip sellers would now refuse to supply neoclouds whose capacity is partly rented to Chinese companies. The BIS rule, which took effect on November 19, replaces a previous limit of 50% of GPUs.

news.title: SAP reportedly considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs to pivot toward AI
news.description: According to Bloomberg, SAP is preparing a plan affecting at least 10,000 positions out of more than 110,000, particularly in product, engineering and sales. The company did not comment, and the figure could change after labor negotiations.

news.title: Meta refuses to let UK regulator test its Muse agent
news.description: The FCA wanted to test Muse in a controlled environment, including observing payments made on consumers’ behalf. Meta declined, even as the agent, already used by more than 10 million people in North America, prepares to launch in the UK.

news.title: X activates parental controls for teens aged 13 to 17
news.description: Teen accounts default to protected mode, with sensitive media restricted and targeted advertising blocked. Parents can limit screen time, approve followers, and filter words without reading messages.

news.title: Group signatures could authenticate photos without identifying their creator
news.description: Cryptographers propose using group signatures to prove that a photo came from a legitimate device without revealing which one. The approach aims to limit the surveillance risk associated with C2PA signatures, but cannot simultaneously guarantee anonymity, revocation and large-scale deployment.

news.title: Latin America attracts AI with its copper and energy
news.description: Demand from data centers and electrification is increasing the value of Chilean copper, Argentine oil and gas, and Brazilian renewables and rare earths. The IEA forecasts that data-center electricity consumption will rise from 485 TWh in 2025 to 950 TWh in 2030.

news.title: TIDAL will remove 29 million fully AI-generated tracks
news.description: TIDAL plans to remove around 29 million tracks generated entirely by AI. The move could improve feed quality, but could also result in human artists’ tracks being removed by mistake.

news.title: Dell reaches $22 billion in revenue from AI servers
news.description: Dell generated $22 billion in AI-server revenue, up 291%. Its order backlog reached $132.3 billion, which could delay some deliveries.

news.title: Claude turns Artifacts creations into Mac and Windows applications
news.description: Claude can convert a creation into a desktop application for Mac or Windows, without packaging or an API key. The beta feature adds icons, shortcuts and notifications, but the applications depend on Claude and may request extensive access to files and the system.

news.title: Microsoft creates Israel-based AI team dedicated to post-quantum security
news.description: Microsoft launched an AI team in Israel tasked with mapping, classifying and fixing vulnerable cryptography. The goal is to help companies prioritize upgrades resistant to quantum computers.

news.title: XPeng’s IRON humanoid robot to be tested in stores in 2027
news.description: XPeng plans to deploy its IRON humanoid robot in its stores in the first quarter of 2027, before a public release in the second quarter. The test is intended to show whether it reduces staff workload or adds new tasks.

news.title: Nvidia 621.40 fixes excessive SSD-writing bug
news.description: The GeForce 621.40 driver targets a background-writing issue that could reach 30 to 40 GB per hour. Users should check which GPUs are affected and inspect their own systems before installing it.

news.title: Google Search uses Wallet data to personalize its responses
news.description: Google Search can now use Google Wallet to provide personalized spending analyses and card recommendations. However, the feature raises privacy concerns, particularly because disconnecting apps does not delete stored Search history.

news.title: Google Meet offers free 1080p video on the Web
news.description: Google Meet now streams 1080p video for free on certain compatible Web setups, without a paid subscription. The feature depends on the computer and browser being used.
